findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets checks entryPointAssetsCache before taking the write lock but never checks it again after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`. If several goroutines observe an empty cache at the same time, each one will acquire the write lock in turn and perform a full manifest read (and, if CDN loading is enabled, an HTTP request) before replacing the global cache. This serializes all late callers behind slow I/O and defeats the cache. It also means a later reload that fails can overwrite an already-populated valid cache with nil, since `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is executed even on error. Re-check `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` immediately after taking the write lock (or use singleflight/double-checked locking) so only the first loader performs the work.

findings.title: No concurrent regression test for the data-race fix
findings.body: This PR exists specifically to fix concurrent access to the global web-assets cache, but no test exercises multiple goroutines calling GetWebAssets while the cache is initially empty and being populated. A race-detector regression test that starts several goroutines against a temporary assets-manifest.json and runs under `go test -race` would verify the synchronization and would also make the missing post-lock cache re-check visible.
